subject.title: fix(codex): stop stale MCP child processes with revalidated SIGKILL escalation

question: Should stale macOS Computer Use MCP children that remain alive for two seconds after SIGTERM be forcibly SIGKILLed by the app-server health monitor?
rationale: The patch deliberately changes the cleanup contract from best-effort SIGTERM to automatic forced termination; source-level PID checks reduce reuse risk but cannot determine whether that lifecycle policy is acceptable for Codex children.

options.title: Approve forced escalation after proof
options.body: Keep the revalidated SIGKILL design once a Codex owner confirms the contract and the contributor adds supported macOS app-server evidence.

options.title: Keep SIGTERM-only cleanup
options.body: Reject automatic forced termination if a surviving child may still own recoverable work or requires a more graceful shutdown protocol.

options.title: Design an explicit lifecycle handshake
options.body: Require a Codex-owned shutdown/health signal before force-killing if the existing child-process contract is not sufficient.

recommendation.title: Approve forced escalation after proof
recommendation.body: Keep the revalidated SIGKILL design once a Codex owner confirms the contract and the contributor adds supported macOS app-server evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: A Codex-area owner is needed to decide whether process escalation is compatible with the intended app-server lifecycle.
